solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fancy brief hot pants, arty, tight

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and the letters reel about drunkenly into a new order

parts.note: H is the short form of hot, as on a tap
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a pair of skimpy, arty, tight hot pants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like a verb or adjective but is a noun, and 'tight' looks like it describes the pants when it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: PHANTASTRY is an archaic noun for imagination or fantasy, the faculty Elizabethans called fancy.

clue.text: Powerful in interstices, it's active withstanding acids etc

definitions.note: describes what the substance does rather than naming it

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other, as something is put into a holder

parts.note: pores are tiny gaps or spaces
hot as in strong or potent

indicators.note: active letters are lively and move about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A powerful agent working in tiny cracks keeps active against acids and similar chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerful' reads as part of the picture, but it is the inner piece; the definition sits at the end and describes what the substance does.
explanation.definitionFit: A photoresist is a light-sensitive coating used in etching circuit boards; the parts it covers resist the acid or other etchant.

clue.text: Clan division in Scots mansion, turning up

parts.note: ha' is the Scots form of hall, a grand house

indicators.note: turning round makes the following word run the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clan split takes place in a Scottish great house, with members turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: A hapu is a Maori subtribe, a section within a larger tribal grouping, so a division of a clan.

clue.text: First of wines included in bill, that is e.g. Beaujolais Nouveau

indicators.note: included in means placed inside another word

parts.note: neb is a bird's bill or beak

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: opening letter of wines
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A wine merchant's bill lists the first of the season's wines, Beaujolais Nouveau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like an invoice but is a bird's beak. Beaujolais Nouveau is the new vintage, a fresh arrival every November.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaujolais Nouveau is the season's freshly released wine, so it is a newcomer, which is what a newbie is.

clue.text: The simplest of sugars I kept in store, granulated?

indicators.note: kept in means held inside the next word
granulated means broken into grains, so the letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone keeps the simplest kind of sugar in store, perhaps the granulated sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A triose is a monosaccharide with just three carbon atoms, the smallest possible sugar molecule.

clue.text: Smooth rock, cut, houses fish inside

indicators.note: something that houses another holds it within its walls
inside confirms the second word goes in the middle too

parts.note: to slice is to cut
ken is old slang for a house, as in boozing ken
id is a variant spelling of ide, a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A smooth stone, once cut, reveals a fossil fish inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' does two jobs: read once it supplies letters from old thieves' slang, read again it signals going inside. Chambers lists the shorter spelling of the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Slickenside is a polished, striated rock surface produced by friction along a geological fault.

clue.text: A racket I'll yield to in sound commercial practice

indicators.note: the letter I gives way, stepping aside so something else takes its place

parts.note: trig is a dialect word for trim, neat, sound
A plus din, a racket

explanation.surface: A sports racket gives way to sound business practice.
explanation.walkthrough: In TRIG the I is replaced by A DIN. Trig is Chambers' word for neat or sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading is buying and selling, the basic activity of commerce.

clue.text: Royal cubit used in measurements

indicators.note: used in means employed within the following word, which contains the answer

parts.note: letters three to seven of this word

explanation.surface: An ancient royal cubit was the unit used in measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: The remen was an ancient Egyptian unit of length, related to the royal cubit.

clue.text: Before playing of test, ball zigzags

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: playing about with a word moves its letters around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Before a Test match, the ball zigzags off the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, which is why ball and zigzags look like bowling; 'Before' just orders the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancettes are zigzag mouldings in architecture, or zigzag lines in heraldry.

clue.text: Oldie's joint, tight and hard

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk, as is tight
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An old person's joint is stiff and hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oldie's' marks the word as archaic, not a reference to an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lith is an obsolete word for a limb or a joint of the body.

clue.text: Gas valve? Bell-end pipe needs adjusting (11, two words)

indicators.note: something that needs adjusting must be reset in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: A plumber notes that the gas valve at the bell-shaped end of a pipe needs adjusting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: the valve lets gas or air out rather than controlling a gas supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleed nipple is a small screw valve on a radiator or brake used to let trapped air or gas escape.

clue.text: Scots dummy to own three quarters of bank

indicators.note: three quarters of a four-letter word keeps three letters and drops the last

parts.note: to own is to have
to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A Scots fool aims to own most of a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Haverel is a Scots word for a fool or someone who talks nonsense; dummy here means a stupid person.

clue.text: One chipping in afterwards backed sale

indicators.note: backed means run backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
chipping in means contributing, joining in among others

parts.note: later means afterwards
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone who contributed later supported a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside LATER, then the whole is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Retail is the selling of goods to the public, so a sale in the sense of trade.

clue.text: Natural substance curbing disease and creating real uproar

parts.note: proper as in genuine, real
a din is a loud noise or uproar

explanation.surface: A natural remedy for disease causes a real stir.
explanation.definitionFit: Properdin is a protein in blood serum that forms part of the immune system's defence against infection.

clue.text: Old composition including a chap in sparkly stuff

indicators.note: including means holding the other words inside

parts.note: dite is an obsolete word for a written composition
A plus man, a chap

explanation.surface: An old piece of writing features a man dressed in glittering clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamante is fabric or decoration covered in glittering fragments like paste diamonds.

clue.text: Bone one removed in cooked trout fish

indicators.note: in means placed within the following word
cooked means prepared or altered, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: removed means taken away from the preceding word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe tells you to bone a trout, then cook the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone' looks like a cook's verb; here it is a word that loses its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large European flatfish prized for eating.

clue.text: Bulk out, as formerly, part of undersize chest

indicators.note: part of means only a section of the following words is used

parts.note: the last letter of the first word and first three of the second

explanation.surface: A tailor pads out part of an undersized chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as formerly' marks the definition as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eche is an old spelling of eke, meaning to increase or supplement.

clue.text: Légumes for Hawaiian dishes

definitions.meaning: second meaning: plural of poi, a paste made from taro root

explanation.surface: Vegetables are served as Hawaiian dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The French accent points to French: pois is the French word for peas, which are légumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pois is French for peas, and poi is the Hawaiian staple of fermented taro paste.

clue.text: Clan leader following son as anti-establishment type

indicators.note: following means coming after the next item named

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
the head of one's kin

explanation.surface: A clan chief succeeding his son turns out to be a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinhead belongs to a youth subculture with shaven heads, associated with defiance of mainstream society.

clue.text: Runners from Bristol on steeplechase

indicators.note: from means taken out of the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Horses running in a steeplechase come from Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests racehorses, which the steeplechase supports; it is a botanical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolons are horizontal stems that creep along the ground and root, which gardeners call runners, as in strawberries.

clue.text: Monetary unit, risen in rank, king struck

indicators.note: struck means struck out, crossed off
in means placed inside the following word

parts.note: rank as a verb means to smell bad, to reek
up as in risen
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A currency has gone up in value, but the king has been struck off its coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like status, but it is the verb meaning to smell foul.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India, Pakistan and several other countries.

clue.text: Tiny element of genetic change, one of pair removed from sheep

indicators.note: removed means taken away from the word

parts.note: mutton is meat from sheep, and an old word for a sheep
one of the doubled letter in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A scientist removes one of a pair of genes from a sheep to make a tiny genetic change.
explanation.definitionFit: A muton is the smallest unit of DNA whose change can produce a mutation.

clue.text: Wine introduced by banquet official, resinous stuff

indicators.note: introduced by means brought in by, put within the following word

parts.note: MC is master of ceremonies
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A toastmaster introduces wine, perhaps a resinated one like retsina.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastic is a resin from a Mediterranean tree, used in varnish and chewing gum.

clue.text: Hauls in warps? Not I, free from such?

indicators.note: warps means twists out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order
not here means leave out the letter named next

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor hauling in warps (mooring ropes) says 'Not me!', wanting to be free of such chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warps' looks like ropes, but is the verb signalling a shuffle. 'such' points back to the ropes in the surface, which is why the definition carries a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlash is to untie something held by lashings, the ropes that warps are.

clue.text: Service, say, including meat I rejected

indicators.note: including means holding the next item inside

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out of the word

parts.note: venison is deer meat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church service, say, features meat that I refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is a common signal for 'for example', abbreviated as two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening church service of the Anglican church.

clue.text: Linked compilation, as present in court

indicators.note: present in means located within the next word

parts.note: to sue is to take to court, as courting a suitor
e.g. means for example, as 'as' can

explanation.surface: A compilation album was presented in court as evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A segue is, among other senses, a sequence of tracks running smoothly into one another.

clue.text: Ray maybe doffing cap, one of pair flanking doorway

indicators.note: doffing your cap takes off what is on top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: the manta is a species of ray

explanation.surface: Someone, perhaps called Ray, doffs his cap at a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name, but it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An anta is a pilaster at the end of a side wall, often one of a pair either side of a temple entrance.

clue.text: Pan reflected rainbow

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, which reads backwards

parts.note: Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow, and iris an old word for one

explanation.surface: The god Pan sees a rainbow reflected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like the god but means the betel leaf chewed in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Siri is betel, the leaf chewed with areca nut, which in India is called pan or paan.

clue.text: Black knight sacrificed by eccentric initially

indicators.note: a sacrificed piece is given up and lost from the board
initially means at the start, so it is the opening letter that goes

parts.note: kinky as in odd or quirky
K is the abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: An eccentric chess player playing Black sacrifices a knight early in the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Inky means as dark as ink, deep black.

clue.text: Numb

parts.note: surface reading: the competition word is given by its plain meaning only
setter's reading: solvers are invited to write their own clue for the word this defines

explanation.walkthrough: This is Azed's competition clue: the setter gives only a definition, and readers submit their own cryptic clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb that has gone to sleep has lost feeling, so it is numb.

clue.text: Latin unseen, perhaps, in hexameters

indicators.note: in means sitting within the following word

parts.note: letters two to five of this word

explanation.surface: A Latin passage to translate at sight might well be in hexameters.
explanation.walkthrough: An unseen is a passage set for translation without preparation, a British school exam term.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin unseen is a form of examination, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Dye, fashionable, worked out, I extend for lining

indicators.note: lining sits inside a garment, so these words go within another

parts.note: in means in fashion
did as in solved, worked out a sum
taken as written
go as in reach, extend, as a road goes to town

explanation.surface: A fashionable dye has been worked out, and I spread it as a lining.
explanation.walkthrough: The inner pair goes in after the first letter of the outer word, not at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigoid dyes are a class of vat dyes chemically related to indigo.

clue.text: Star swallows cocktail — it's gone down fast! (6, two words)

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower

parts.note: the sun is a star
kir is white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: A celebrity downs a cocktail in one gulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone down fast' reads as the drink being gulped, but describes skiers descending a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski run is a slope skiers descend at speed, so it is something gone down fast.

clue.text: As Jock's day progresses, energy goes into diversion of ladies

indicators.note: goes into means enters the next item
a diversion sends things off a direct route, so the letters are redirected

parts.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: As a Scotsman's day goes on, his energy turns to entertaining women.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scot, so the definition points to a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Deiseal means sunwise, clockwise, the direction the sun moves through the day.

clue.text: Marks on cheesy men after damaging skin tissue

definitions.note: loose: mesenchyme is embryonic tissue that develops into the dermis among others

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cheesy men leave marks on someone after damaging their skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesenchyme is loose embryonic connective tissue from which the dermis, bone and blood develop.
